text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000018 bills 99215 far above its risk-adjusted expectation, but the small documented sample supports the billed levels, so the pattern is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess persists after risk adjustment and appears in every complexity stratum: the 99215 share runs roughly two to five times the all-provider share even for patients with 0 to 2 conditions. That is a pattern consistent with a level-selection habit rather than panel acuity alone, although most 99215s do fall on patients with 5 or more conditions. Against this, none of the 9 documented 99215 claims were coded below the billed level (examples C0012304 and C0012510 show high MDM with about 50 minutes). However, 9 charts out of a roughly 5.6% records return is too thin to clear the provider, and only 2 of 23 notes show the possible-inflation signal, which is weak. A reviewer should first pull charts for the low-complexity 99215s, especially C0012483 and C0012524 (the same 0-condition patient, billed for back pain and a UTI code) and C0012538 (a Z09 follow-up only). The reviewer should then request a larger documentation sample of 99215 and 99214 claims to test whether the clean documentation holds up and whether notes look templated."}
